audience.role: A DSH user who already runs the plugin and is deciding whether to take this version, and a first-time repository reader

checks.note: The README answers whether this release is for the reader and how to install it; the changelog answers what changed between 0.5.0 and 0.5.1 and what the upgrade requires. Neither duplicates the other: the README lists no per-change detail, and the changelog restates no installation step.

A reader can state that 0.5.1 moves to DSH >= 0.1.5-rc.1, that the old Session API is gone with no fallback, that the required action is to start a new session rather than migrate anything, that the native gate for this host has not been run, and that 0.5.1 itself is not published yet so the unpinned install is the one that works today.

Internal terms arrive after the effect they describe. "Host lock" follows the inspect/inject commands that produce it, and "registry-derived" is introduced with its plain meaning - the rows are published npm tarball identities and no host has loaded the graph - before the digest consequence is stated.

The candidate changelog distinguishes a real host loop with a simulated model from native application and real-model acceptance. README identifies the package as unpublished and the native audit as pending. The added recovery guidance does not imply release of the reserved action.

The README leads with installation and states that host-lock injection follows the runtime upgrade. The candidate changelog explains compatibility and pending-confirmation recovery, then unchanged guarantees and separate acceptance gates.

Both Chinese editions stand on their own: commands and version identifiers are preserved verbatim, and the Chinese prose states the same facts and the same required action without depending on the English text.

findings.message: The structural auditor warns that the status paragraph names exact versions. This is the current compatibility level rather than historical provenance, and the paragraph links docs/COMPATIBILITY.md for the full record of the range, the prerelease rules, and the exact graph. The Chinese edition carries the same warning at README.zh-CN.md:52 and the same link.

limitations: Candidate follow-up: cold-read the updated English and Chinese 0.5.1 entries and the unchanged README entry paths. The new wait-recovery bullet and simulated-model fixture boundary are clear in both languages. Historical entries retain their previous review scope.
The cold read covered the four reader documents that changed for 0.5.1. The long-form acceptance record and the compatibility reference were checked for factual consistency, not re-read end to end.
This receipt binds the working-tree bytes at review time. Any later edit to a listed document invalidates it and requires a fresh cold read.
A passing receipt records that the review happened; it does not establish factual correctness, native acceptance, or publication.
